items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: When Josephine Baker first came to New York, I was playing with Buddy Rich and they hired Buddy Rich’s band to accompany her in the theatres in New York

ctx.x: Can we backtrack and little and discuss how you settled in Los Angeles and how you ended up making this your home.

When Josephine Baker first came to New York, I was playing with Buddy Rich and they hired Buddy Rich’s band to accompany her in the theatres in New York, I think it was the Strand. And she suggested that we do a little act together. So, she showed me on this little tune (sings)… it’s got a little Latin beat to it. And she says, “I want you to come down when I start singing and you make a few little notes on your horn and I’ll do a little dance to that and few little notes again..” We rehearsed it and got it down…
What year was that would you say?

items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: And then she went back to Paris and came back the next year and I became her musical director. That was in 1952. Oh, I toured with her for a long time.

ctx.x: Well, 1950, when Josephine Baker first came over to the States. Buddy Rich, we were backing Josephine Baker. He became her musical director. And the band. So from about, oh, about four months we toured with Josephine Baker and then Buddy, you know, it was just theaters. Buddy wanted to play, naturally everybody wanted to play. But Buddy Rich is not the type to be an accompanist, you know. So he split and I became

the trumpet player with her, you know. And then she went back to Paris and came back the next year and I became her musical director. That was in 1952. Oh, I toured with her for a long time. Went to Mexico City six months.
